geodetic-control-networks.title: Geodesy and geodetic control networks
geodetic-control-networks.summary: Reference points with known coordinates that tie every later measurement on a project together.
geodetic-control-networks.metaTitle: Geodetic control networks and GNSS control points — MAES17
geodetic-control-networks.metaDescription: Establishing and densifying geodetic control: GNSS and total station observations, network adjustment and coordinate lists for surveys and construction.
geodetic-control-networks.intro: A control network is a set of marked points whose coordinates are determined precisely. Topographic surveys, boundary work and construction layout all depend on it for consistency.
when: Before a large survey or construction project starts
When existing reference points are missing, damaged or unreliable
When several teams must work in one coordinate system
deliverables: Coordinate and height list of control points
Point descriptions with sketches or photos

land-surveying.title: Land surveying and dimensional measurements
land-surveying.summary: Measurements of plots, buildings and features for planning, design and documentation.
land-surveying.metaTitle: Land surveying and measurement services — MAES17
land-surveying.metaDescription: Measurement of land plots, buildings and site features with coordinate-based plans and dimensions prepared for planning, design and documentation.
land-surveying.intro: Land surveying records the position and dimensions of plots, buildings, fences, roads and other features, producing a measured plan of the site as it exists.
when: Planning a purchase, sale or division of land
Preparing for design or renovation work
Checking the actual dimensions of a plot or building
includes: Measurement of plot outlines and features
Tie-in to a defined coordinate system

topographic-surveying.title: Topographic surveying and terrain mapping
topographic-surveying.summary: Plans of terrain relief and site features, with heights and contours, for design and construction.
topographic-surveying.metaTitle: Topographic surveys and terrain mapping — MAES17
topographic-surveying.metaDescription: Topographic surveys with contours, spot heights, utilities and site features. Digital terrain models and plans at the scale your designer needs.
topographic-surveying.intro: A topographic survey shows the shape of the ground and everything on it: heights, slopes, buildings, roads, trees and visible utilities. It is the base drawing for most design work.
when: Before architectural, road or landscape design
When calculating earthwork volumes
When planning drainage or site grading
includes: Measurement of spot heights and break lines
Survey of buildings, roads and visible utilities
Digital terrain model and contour generation
deliverables: Topographic plan at an agreed scale
Contour lines and spot heights in CAD format

cadastral-surveying.title: Cadastral surveying and property boundary determination
cadastral-surveying.summary: Surveys that identify and document property boundaries for registration, transactions and disputes.
cadastral-surveying.metaTitle: Cadastral surveys and property boundary determination — MAES17
cadastral-surveying.metaDescription: Boundary surveys for land plots: comparing documents with the situation on site, determining boundary points and preparing materials for registration.
cadastral-surveying.intro: Cadastral surveying compares legal documents with the situation on the ground and determines the position of property boundaries and boundary points.
when: Registering, dividing or merging land plots
Buying or selling property
Resolving uncertainty about where a boundary lies
includes: Review of title documents and existing cadastral data
Comparison of measured and documented boundaries
deliverables: Materials prepared for submission, where applicable

construction-surveying.title: Construction surveying and setting-out
construction-surveying.summary: Transferring design positions and levels to the site, and checking construction as it progresses.
construction-surveying.metaDescription: Setting-out of buildings, axes and levels from design drawings, construction control measurements and checks of built elements during the works.
construction-surveying.intro: Construction surveying puts the design on the ground: building corners, axes, levels and reference lines are marked so construction follows the approved plan.
when: At the start of foundation and structural works
When axes and levels must be transferred between floors
When the contractor or client needs independent checks
includes: Setting-out of axes, corners and levels
Checks of built elements against design

land-management.title: Land management and land development
land-management.summary: Spatial planning and documentation for using, dividing and developing land.
land-management.metaTitle: Land management and land development services — MAES17
land-management.metaDescription: Land management work: plot division and consolidation plans, land use documentation and spatial data for development projects.
land-management.intro: Land management organises how land is used and divided. It combines survey data with planning requirements to prepare plot layouts and supporting documentation.
when: Dividing or consolidating land plots
Preparing land for development
Changing or documenting land use
includes: Analysis of existing land data and constraints

as-built-surveys.title: As-built surveys and technical documentation
as-built-surveys.summary: Recording what was actually built, for acceptance, registration and future maintenance.
as-built-surveys.metaTitle: As-built surveys and technical documentation — MAES17
as-built-surveys.metaDescription: As-built surveys of buildings, structures and site works, compared with design, with drawings and documentation for acceptance and records.
as-built-surveys.intro: An as-built survey records the final position and dimensions of constructed buildings, utilities and site works so they can be compared with the design and documented.
when: Completing a construction project
Before registering a new or altered building
When reliable records of existing structures are missing
includes: Measurement of completed structures and site works

engineering-surveying.title: Engineering and specialised surveying
engineering-surveying.summary: Surveys for roads, utilities, slopes and other engineering tasks with specific accuracy needs.
engineering-surveying.metaDescription: Engineering surveys for roads, utilities, slopes and structures: profiles, cross-sections, volume calculations and repeated monitoring measurements.
engineering-surveying.intro: Engineering surveying supports design and maintenance of infrastructure. It covers tasks such as longitudinal profiles, cross-sections, volume calculations and repeated measurements of movement.
when: Designing roads, pipelines or other linear works
Calculating earthwork or stockpile volumes
Observing movement of slopes or structures over time
